source_review.notes: Reviewed current C++ vector draft clauses, Rust Vec and Rustonomicon documentation, Java SE 25 ArrayList contract, Go append specification and slice internals, CPython list source and C API, and .NET List capacity documentation. All eleven final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked buffer/length/capacity/maximum, live/spare half-open ranges, utilization, required/new capacity, cost, potential, and capacity-trace notation for consistent domains.
Separated unit element work, byte traffic, allocator cost, peak storage, actual operation latency, and amortized cost.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Amortized is never used as a synonym for probabilistic average or per-operation worst case.

evidence: Replayed nine appends: capacity trace (1,2,4,4,8,8,8,8,16), copied elements 1+2+4+8=15, and total modeled writes 15+9=24.
Checked the final live prefix contains exactly 0 through 8, length is 9, capacity is 16, and all seven spare slots retain the educational marker.
Checked 2^63 doubled in unsigned 64-bit arithmetic reaches 2^64 and cannot be represented, supporting the overflow example.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite modeled counters do not establish runtime timing or general asymptotic behavior.

evidence: Re-derived geometric sum 1+2+...+2^(m-1)=2^m-1 and the fewer-than-N copied-element bound for N successful appends.
Recomputed potential Phi=2n-c+1: spare append actual 1 plus delta 2 gives 3; full append actual n+1 plus delta 2-n also gives 3.
Checked the general factor tradeoff and hysteresis charging argument while retaining rounding and threshold proof obligations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The general geometric statement assumes a factor bounded away from one and guaranteed capacity progress.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one capacity, exact-full and just-over boundaries, bulk required sizes, maximum capacity/bytes, zero-sized types, allocation failure, self-alias input, and throwing/move-only/resource-owning elements.

Reviewed partial transfer rollback, old/new peak memory, iterator/pointer/slice/FFI invalidation, conditional Go slice aliasing, insertion/erase shifts, retained removed data, explicit shrink, and capacity-policy version changes.

Reviewed grow/shrink thrashing, migration frontier, allocation/page latency, concurrent publication/races, untrusted lengths, exhaustion, remanence, asynchronous consumers, and clinical/system deadline boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Incremental copying is not claimed to bound allocator, initialization, page, callback, synchronization, or total operation latency automatically.

evidence: At every committed state 0<=length<=capacity<=maximum, live slots encode the abstract sequence, and spare slots are not live elements.
Append publishes length only after construction; growth commits one valid representation or applies its documented failure guarantee with exactly-once cleanup.
Aliases and observers follow operation-specific invalidation, and growth/shrink claims remain bound to their actual policy.
invariant_checking.notes: Private implementation growth constants are not promoted to public cross-version contracts.

evidence: Reviewed spare and full append cases against abstraction preservation and transactional ownership transfer.
Reviewed aggregate and potential proofs against initial capacity, unit-cost, successful-operation, rounding, and reachable-state assumptions.
Reviewed hysteresis and deamortization discussions for missing transition, buffer-selection, allocation, failure, iterator, and concurrency obligations.
proof_review.notes: The proofs do not establish a production allocator, element type, library growth policy, hard deadline, or peak resident-memory bound.

evidence: Geometric and potential derivations identify their cost model and explicitly distinguish observed traces from proofs.
Performance, incremental migration, concurrency, security, and clinical claims are scoped as conditional design/evidence obligations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No finite trace or amortized theorem is represented as deployment, denial-of-service, real-time, or safety certification.

evidence: The standard-library Python snippet passed exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_growth_trace_not_complexity_proof, and all eleven source destinations plus all local links were directly checked.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production vector/list/slice, allocator, generic element transfer, failure injection, invalidation, memory peak, concurrency, or runtime performance was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed abstract/live/spare state, transactional append, unspecified growth policy, checked capacity, aggregate/potential analysis, latency/peak space, reserve, invalidation/aliasing, insertion/erasure, retention/shrink, hysteresis, deamortization, testing/measurement, concurrency, security, and high-stakes boundaries.
